solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: African city to repair, ruined (8)

indicators.note: something ruined is broken up, so the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A city in such bad shape that fixing it seems hopeless.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks you to fix something; the fodder is the phrase that tells you to fix it.
annotation.definitionFit: Pretoria is South Africa's administrative capital.

entries.clue: Wet, bottom piece of hosiery got hitched up (4)

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its final letter
in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: last letter of hosierY
to get hitched is to marry

annotation.surface: A stocking pulled up while soaking wet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hitched up' looks like hoisting a stocking, but 'hitched' is the wedding and 'up' flips the whole string, Y included.
annotation.definitionFit: Covered in dew means lightly wet, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Putridness originally in no longer fresh bread and butter (6)

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, so its first letter
one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: stale = no longer fresh
first letter of Putridness, put inside STA…LE

annotation.surface: Old bread going off, with its butter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bread and butter' reads as food beside the stale loaf, but as one phrase it means a basic, regular thing.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone's bread and butter is the basic item they rely on, their mainstay.

entries.clue: Container, trap for wordplayers? (6)

blocks.note: a small basket, of the kind soft fruit is sold in
a net to catch people who make puns; the question mark flags an invented sense

annotation.surface: A box for catching people who love puns.
annotation.walkthrough: A punnet is the small plastic or card basket that strawberries are sold in. Split as PUN NET, it becomes a net for punsters.
annotation.definitionFit: The first sense is a real container for berries; the second is a made-up compound, PUN + NET.

entries.clue: Very difficult angle cornering I conclude (8)

indicators.note: to corner something is to hem it in, so FISH goes around the rest

blocks.note: to angle is to fish
to conclude is to end
I as written, placed after END inside FI…SH

annotation.surface: A tricky geometry problem you finally solve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Angle' looks geometric, and 'cornering' goes with it, but here angle is the verb for fishing with a rod. The inserted pair is read END then I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a puzzle described as devilishly hard is one only a fiend could set.

entries.clue: Various takers for succession (6)

indicators.note: various arrangements of the letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: Several rivals lining up to inherit a throne.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Succession' suggests heirs, and 'takers' fits that picture, but here succession means an unbroken run.
annotation.definitionFit: A winning streak is an unbroken succession of wins.

entries.clue: Put in established pattern, decorative design (7) milky mist (7)

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: rote = a fixed, repeated routine
to set is to put; SET goes inside RO…TE
not part of this clue: stray text from another clue picked up when the puzzle was copied

annotation.surface: Placing an ornament into a set scheme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put in' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'Put' is SET and 'in' is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A rosette is a rose-shaped decorative design, carved or made of ribbon.

entries.clue: Stumbles in area of field (5)

blocks.note: loses footing, a verb
a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper

annotation.surface: Someone tripping over in a meadow.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket, the slips are the fielders standing beside the wicketkeeper to catch edges, and the part of the field where they stand.
annotation.definitionFit: One word, two senses: a verb for stumbling and a cricket term for a region of the field.

entries.clue: Left port, sea’s choppy (2,5)

indicators.note: a choppy sea is broken up, like the letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A ship has left harbour into rough water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left port' looks like a sailing report, and 'port' is also the left side of a ship; neither sense is used, as port is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Left in the sense of remaining over: with time to spare means with time left.

entries.clue: Holidaymaker in suit or pants, cap in turquoise (7)

indicators.note: British slang for rubbish, so the letters are made a mess of
the cap of a word is its top, so its first letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters
first letter of Turquoise

annotation.surface: A holidaymaker dressed in a suit or trousers with a turquoise hat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like clothing beside 'suit' and 'cap', but in British slang pants means rubbish.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone on holiday somewhere is a visitor, a tourist.

entries.clue: Dry days in September, including first of that month? (7)

indicators.note: one piece takes another inside it
the first of a word is the letter it starts with

blocks.note: September has thirty days
first letter of September, put inside THIR…TY

annotation.surface: A question about a dry spell in early September.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First of that month' reads as the date 1 September, but it means the first letter of the month's name.
annotation.definitionFit: Dry in the sense of wanting a drink, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Punishment, writer given cane, unfortunately (7)

indicators.note: things going wrong, so the letters are out of place

blocks.note: a pen is a writer, the tool that writes
anagram fodder, 4 letters

annotation.surface: A writer being caned as a punishment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but crosswords often mean the pen itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Penance is a punishment taken on to atone for wrongdoing.

entries.clue: Overcome a verbose drunk grabbing yours truly (4,5)

indicators.note: a drunk staggers, so the letters are all over the place
the anagram takes hold of the next piece

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
yours truly = the setter = I, taken inside

annotation.surface: Coping with a wordy drunk who grabs hold of you.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Yours truly' is the setter's way of saying I or ME.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to get the better of a difficulty or insult without being dragged down by it.

entries.clue: Blade from hero, a rapier (3)

indicators.note: the answer is taken from the letters that follow

blocks.note: herO A Rapier

annotation.surface: A swashbuckler's sword taken from the hero.
annotation.walkthrough: Blade and rapier both say sword, but the blade meant is the flat end of an oar.
annotation.definitionFit: Part for whole: the flat end of an oar is its blade, and rowers call the whole oar a blade.

entries.clue: Figure revealed by growth in kilos (5)

indicators.note: the answer shows itself within the words

blocks.note: growTH IN Kilos

annotation.surface: Weight gain showing up on someone's figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like the body in this dieting picture, but it is the verb, as in 'I figure so'.
annotation.definitionFit: Figure as a verb, as in 'I figure it will rain', means to reckon or suppose.

entries.clue: For atop head, that off immediately! (2,3,4,2,1,3)

annotation.answer: AT THE DROP OF A HAT

indicators.note: letters that are off are out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: An order to take the hat off your head at once.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder describes a hat and 'off' is an order to remove it, so the surface itself acts out the dropping of a hat.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for doing something instantly, without hesitation.

entries.clue: Figure you smooth down (8)

blocks.note: thou is the old word for you
to sand wood is to smooth it down

annotation.surface: Someone told to smooth down their figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' reads as shape or body, but it means a number.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a thousand is one of many numbers, and numbers are figures.

entries.clue: Go off, old man (3)

blocks.note: what a balloon or a cork does, with a bang
informal for father, one's old man

annotation.surface: Telling an elderly man to leave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is informal for father; pop is another such word.
annotation.definitionFit: One word, two senses: a small bang, and a familiar name for a dad.

entries.clue: Vulnerable, newspaper having opened dossier (7)

indicators.note: the newspaper has opened the dossier and gone inside it

blocks.note: a dossier is a file of papers
a rag is a low-quality newspaper; it goes inside F…ILE

annotation.surface: A person exposed after a paper has read their secret file.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rag' is a scornful word for a newspaper.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: easily broken or hurt.

entries.clue: Formal gathering disconnected, still upset about that (3,5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, set upwards means read from bottom to top
one piece goes around another

blocks.note: YET = still, turned upwards to give TEY
apart = disconnected; it sits inside TE…Y

annotation.surface: Someone still upset about being cut off at a formal event.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still upset' reads as ongoing annoyance, but 'still' is YET and 'upset' turns it over. 'That' points back to APART.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an afternoon tea with invited guests is one kind of social gathering.

entries.clue: Point where reggae initially gets suffocated by funk (5)

indicators.note: at the start, so the word's opening letter
it is smothered, so wrapped inside the other piece

blocks.note: funk can mean a strong smell, and a pong is a stink
first letter of Reggae, inside P…ONG

annotation.surface: The moment in a set where reggae gets drowned out by funk music.
annotation.walkthrough: Funk and reggae both look like music, but funk also means a bad smell; pong is British for stink.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: each spike of a fork is a point.

entries.clue: Fragrant cream prepared, topped by shell of pistachio (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece that follows goes on top
the shell of a word is its outer letters

blocks.note: outer letters of PistachiO
made = prepared

annotation.surface: Pistachio ice cream topped with crushed shells.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cream' and 'pistachio' make a dessert, but the cream here is a scented hair ointment.
annotation.definitionFit: A scented ointment for styling hair, so a fragrant cream.

entries.clue: Good field for country house (6)

blocks.note: G = good
a field of study is its range or scope

annotation.surface: A fine plot of land for a country house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Field' reads as farmland in this rural picture, but it means scope or range.
annotation.definitionFit: A British term for a country house with farm buildings attached.

entries.clue: Head honcho on hand? (3,6)

blocks.note: the surface reading: the boss, slang for the person in charge
the setter's reading: a hand is a bunch of bananas, and the head one sits at the top

annotation.surface: A boss who is always available.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On hand' reads as available, but a hand is also a bunch of bananas, so the top one of the hand is the head banana.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal term for the most important person, the boss, read literally as the fruit at the top of a hand.

entries.clue: Pint-sized, having had a few pints? (6)

blocks.note: very small
slightly drunk

annotation.surface: A small person who has been drinking.
annotation.walkthrough: Tiddly is British slang with both senses: tiny, and a little tipsy.
annotation.definitionFit: One informal British word with two senses, tiny and tipsy.

entries.clue: A minor injury, athlete’s foot severe (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the foot of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: A as written
a cut is a minor injury
last letter of athletE

annotation.surface: A runner downplaying a nasty foot fungus.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Athlete's foot' is the fungal infection in the surface; the wordplay only wants the last letter of 'athlete'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as said of pain or a shortage that is intense.

entries.clue: Yellowish-brown dirt orbiting sun (7)

indicators.note: to orbit something is to circle it, so MUD goes around

blocks.note: mud = dirt
the sun is a star; STAR goes inside MU…D

annotation.surface: A brownish dusty planet circling the sun.
annotation.walkthrough: The sun is a star, so here it gives STAR rather than the usual abbreviation S.
annotation.definitionFit: A colour named after the condiment, a dull yellow with brown in it.

entries.clue: Greek character in April recollected flower (7)

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another
gathered up again, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: mu is the Greek letter M
anagram fodder, 5 letters, with MU inside

annotation.surface: Someone remembering a Greek figure and a flower from one April.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' reads as remembered, but split as re-collected it means gathered up afresh.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the primula is a spring flower of the primrose family.

entries.clue: Fairy king with goblet raised (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means written from bottom to top

blocks.note: K = king, as in chess
a goblet is a drinking cup; K + CUP then reads upwards

annotation.surface: A fairy king lifting his goblet in a toast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fairy king' suggests Oberon, but the definition is only 'Fairy'. Puck serves Oberon in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Puck is the mischievous fairy of English folklore and Shakespeare.

entries.clue: Single girl behind daughter in Irish county (7)

indicators.note: the following pieces come after D

blocks.note: D = daughter
single = one
gal = girl

annotation.surface: An unmarried woman trailing her daughter around Ireland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Single girl' reads as an unmarried woman, but the two words are separate pieces, and 'behind' puts both after the daughter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Donegal is a county in the far north-west of Ireland.

entries.clue: Fair head of lady cushioned by setter? (7)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top, so its first letter
held inside, as if padded all round

blocks.note: cement is something that sets
first letter of Lady, inside C…EMENT

annotation.surface: A pale-haired woman leaning on the person who wrote the crossword.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is cement, which sets hard; the question mark flags it.
annotation.definitionFit: Said of weather, fair and mild; a plain synonym in that sense.
